evidence.title: Bernard de Wisk
evidence.text: Bernard de Wisk was a mercenary captain and sometime brigand of the Hundred Years War.

evidence.title: Bernard de Wisk
evidence.text: Wisk started out a mercenary, However, after the Treaty of Brétigny was signed on May 8, 1360, Wisk found himself unemployed and so turned to Brigandry.

evidence.title: Bernard de Wisk

evidence.title: Bernard de Wisk
evidence.text: In 1369, with Bernardon and Hortingo de la Salle, he seized Belleperche Castle, home to Isabella of Valois, Duchess of Bourbon, mother- in- law of the king, Charles V of France and demanded a ransom.

evidence.title: Bernard de Wisk
evidence.text: The castle was, however, besieged by the troops of the Dukes of Bourbon and Burgundy.

evidence.title: Bernard de Wisk
evidence.text: The Duke of Bourbon( Louis II, Duke of Bourbon) was her son, and John Frossart tells us that the siege redoubt he organized was as strong and as well fortified as a good town might have been.

evidence.title: Bernard de Wisk
evidence.text: The" Free companies" in the castle were expelled, but they took the duchess with them as hostage.

evidence.title: Bernard de Wisk
evidence.text: The Duchess remained a prisoner until 1372, when the king arranged for the ransom to be paid.

evidence.title: Charles, Count of Valois
evidence.text: Charles of Valois (12 March 1270 – 16 December 1325), the third son of Philip III of France and Isabella of Aragon, was a member of the House of Capet and founder of the House of Valois, whose rule over France would start in 1328.

evidence.title: Charles, Count of Valois
evidence.text: Charles ruled several principalities.

evidence.text: He held in appanage the counties of Valois, Alençon and Perche.

evidence.title: Charles, Count of Valois

evidence.title: Charles, Count of Valois
evidence.text: Through his marriage to Catherine I, titular empress of the Latin Empire, he was titular Latin Emperor of Constantinople from 1301–1307, although he ruled from exile and only had authority over Crusader States in Greece.

evidence.title: Charles, Count of Valois
evidence.text: The grandson of Louis IX of France, Charles of Valois was a son, brother, brother-in-law and son-in-law of kings or queens (of France, Navarre, England and Naples).

evidence.title: Charles, Count of Valois
evidence.text: His descendants, the House of Valois, would become the royal house of France three years after his death, beginning with his son Philip VI of France.
